MECHANISM. The let-init iterator-cursor folds (iter/adapters/{skip,filter,enumerate,filter_map,skip_while}.rs *_fold) are `<lit-array>.iter().<adaptor>().fold/rfold(<init>, |acc, &x| { assert_eq!(x, ys[acc..]); .. })` over LITERAL xs/ys. The defolder (decompose_fold -> FoldSugar) ALREADY threads the accumulator over the finite element sequence and digs the in-place case; it declined these on (a) the fold ACC-INIT being `ys.len()` / `xs.len() - 1` -- a literal-array length is not an int LITERAL, so const_int(init) returned None and the whole defold bailed to the 'let-initializer' refusal; and (b) the skip_while/filter predicate `|&x| *x < 15` -- the `*x` deref was outside const_eval's closed set.
  FIX (3 surgical, all EXACT-OR-BAIL):
  (1) const_int_acc_init(expr, let_inits): a SCOPE-AWARE acc-init resolver -- int literal | `<lit-array>.len()` (-> element count, resolved through let_inits via literal_array_len_with_lets) | `+`/`-`/`*` arithmetic over those (`xs.len() - 1`). THE LAW: over a literal domain the cursor START position is itself a literal in scope. A runtime `.len()` / non-arithmetic op returns None -> the defold declines (safe under-claim). Wired into decompose_fold's acc_0 only.
  (2) const_eval `*x` (UnOp::Deref): the const model holds scalar VALUES (no pointers) and a `&x`/`&&x` param binds the dereferenced element, so `*x` is the identity on that value -- faithful, lets the skip_while/filter predicate const-evaluate. (+2: the two skip_while.rs `|&x| *x<15` cursor folds.)
  (3) resolve_index_in_formula (TEETH): after the accumulator (the index) is threaded to a concrete literal, a body `index(ys, <const>)` over a CAPTURED literal array (FoldSugar.literal_arrays, owned from let_inits at decompose time) is rewritten to its concrete element TERM (with const_fold_int_term folding `sub(4,1)` -> 3 first). This is what makes a wrong-expected twin z3-REFUTABLE: the asserted RHS carries the REAL element value (`6==99`) instead of the always-SAT uninterpreted EUF accessor (`6==index(ys,3)`). SCOPED to the fold body -- no other already-discharged site's lifted form changes (CID/refused both held; the index resolution is a localized strengthening, OOB/unknown-array index left as the EUF floor).

+7 = +5 (acc-init `.len()` resolution: skip.rs x2 rfold, filter.rs x1 rfold, enumerate.rs x1 rfold[xs.len()-1], filter_map.rs x1 rfold) + +2 (skip_while.rs `*x` deref predicate). The forward `.fold(0, ..)` cursor cases already dug on main (acc-init was the literal 0).

HONESTLY NOT DRAINED (correct disposition, NOT forced -- an honest non-drain beats a fake-dig): the OTHER bin-1 'opportunity' buckets are NOT soundly diggable and STAY refused/unclassified -- fmt/mod.rs (body asserts read RUNTIME accessors `fmt.flags()&1`, loop var only on the RHS), iter/traits/iterator.rs (`v.iter().nth(i)` runtime iterator method + `let mut iter; iter.advance_by(i)` intervening mutation), num/flt2dec/{dragon,grisu}.rs (mutated accumulator `prevpow10`/`prevtenk` + runtime fns), the try_fold(f) comparisons (runtime fn `f`), zip.rs/cloned.rs `.any(|v| &xs==*v)` (compared `xs`/`count` are runtime). filter_map's *_fold stays bin-2 (filter_map Option const-eval is the established inexact-adaptor bail). These are runtime-value or un-nameable-cursor cases -- digging them would be a FAKE-DISCHARGE. EFFECT-OR-LEAVE held: only a value provably reducible to a literal element over a statically-determinable cursor was dug.

TermBreadthSugar (-34): three term-path sub-fixes in translate_term_in_scope. (A) FLOAT CASTS: scalar_cast_type_key recognizes f16/f32/f64/f128, so `expr as f32` emits opaque EUF `cast:f32(<expr>)` (IEEE width in the ctor NAME only, no Real semantics); drains num/mod.rs float<->float round-trips incl. the two `infinity as f32` rows (cast receiver now lifts inside translate_infinity_eq_assertion). `neg_zero as f32 == -0.0f32` stays unclassified (signed-zero IEEE guard, untouched). Only the WRAPPER is transparent: `unsafe { &mut *cell.get() }` still bails.
